requirements.quote: Preference is given to students with strong backgrounds in both biology and a quantitative science, but this need not be demonstrated with a double major.

problems: No specific mathematics/statistics/programming courses are named on any CSB page checked (home, admissions, FAQ, about, curriculum) or in the MIT catalog entry (catalog.mit.edu/interdisciplinary/graduate-programs/computational-systems-biology/); the only expectation is a preference for a strong background in a quantitative science.

About page / catalog: 'Applicants must have an undergraduate degree in biology (or a related field), bioinformatics, chemistry, computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics, or an engineering discipline' - a degree-field requirement, not a math coursework requirement, so not recorded as one.
Admissions page lists application materials only (transcripts, letters, statement); no course prerequisites.
